title: Mission Proposal & Approval
description: The agent proposes a mission to the Person Server: a Markdown description of what it intends to accomplish, the tools it wants, and the resources it expects to use. Because the PS acts for a person, approval is deferred — 202, then polling while the person reviews. On approval the PS returns {s256, mission, capabilities, person_tokens}: the mission blob base64url-encoded so its digest covers unambiguous bytes, and one mission-scoped person token per approved resource.

mission_blob.title: Approved Mission Blob
mission_blob.description: The bytes the PS persisted and returned base64url-encoded as the `mission` member. s256 is the digest of those bytes.
mission_blob.markdown:
# Analyze Q2 Customer Feedback

Read customer feedback records and produce a summary report with sentiment analysis and key themes.

approved_tools.name: ReportWriter
approved_tools.description: Write the summary report to the shared drive

steps.label: Discover PS metadata
annotations: The agent fetches PS well-known metadata to discover the endpoints it needs.
mission_endpoint is where the agent proposes missions, and where it later POSTs updates and its completion proposal at {mission_endpoint}/{mission_s256}.
person_token_endpoint is REQUIRED in -11: every PS MUST publish one and MUST issue person tokens from it.
auth_token_endpoint was called token_endpoint before -11.
mission_control_endpoint is the control plane — where parties other than the owning agent read and manage missions. Its operations are left to a companion specification.

steps.label: POST /mission (sig=jwt) → 202 + interaction URL

request_body.description:
# Analyze Q2 Customer Feedback

Read customer feedback records and produce a summary report with sentiment analysis and key themes.

tools.name: ReportWriter
tools.description: Write the summary report to the shared drive

annotations: The agent POSTs the mission proposal signed with its agent token (sig=jwt). The body carries a content-digest, so content-type and content-digest are covered components too.
description is Markdown. tools and resources are OPTIONAL.

resources names the resources the agent expects to use. The PS presents them to the person alongside the description and issues a person token for each it approves — the list is not a limit on the mission.
The PS cannot approve without the person, so it returns 202 Accepted with a pending URL and an interaction URL.
AAuth-Capabilities is not used on PS endpoints; the agent passes capabilities in the request body instead.

steps.label: Poll /pending/m3f7a1b2 → 202 (user hasn't approved yet)
annotations: Agent polls the pending URL from the Location header.
PS returns 202 — the user has not yet reviewed or approved the mission.
Agent waits Retry-After seconds before polling again.

steps.label: User reviews mission → approves
steps.response_body:
Review Agent Mission

Analyze Q2 Customer Feedback

The agent aauth:local@agent.example is requesting approval for the following mission:

Read customer feedback records and produce a summary report with sentiment analysis and key themes.

Tools the agent will use:

  • FeedbackReader — Read customer feedback records
  • ReportWriter — Write the summary report to the shared drive
annotations: User opens the interaction URL (from PS notification, email, or app).
PS displays the mission description and full tool list for review.
User reads what the agent intends to do and which tools it will use.
User clicks Approve — PS marks the mission as approved.
Per §1224 the PS or user MAY refine the description/tools here before approval — the approved blob can differ from the proposal.

steps.label: Poll /pending/m3f7a1b2 → 200 + approval response
annotations: The person approved — the next poll returns 200 with the approval response.
The response is {s256, mission, capabilities, person_tokens}. It is NOT the bare blob: -11 moved the blob into a base64url `mission` member so the digest covers an unambiguous byte sequence.

The agent decodes `mission`, computes SHA-256 over the decoded bytes, and compares the unpadded base64url result to `s256`. Verification is a SHOULD, and the agent may then store the mission however it likes.
capabilities is NOT part of the blob and is not covered by the digest. It says whether the PS can currently reach the person — this moment, not a term of the mission.
person_tokens is present because the proposal named `resources`: one mission-scoped person token per approved resource, each carrying mission_s256, sparing the agent a request each.
The blob carries approver, agent, approved_at and description as a floor, and MAY carry expires_at, approved_tools and approved_resources. A reader ignores members it does not recognize.

events.label: Proposal submitted
events.detail: PS queues mission for user review, returns pending URL + interaction URL

events.label: Still awaiting approval
events.detail: User has not yet opened the interaction URL

events.label: User approves
events.detail: User reviews mission description and tool list, clicks Approve

events.label: Mission approved
events.detail: PS returns {s256, mission, capabilities, person_tokens}; the agent verifies s256 against the decoded mission bytes

s256_chain.label: Mission blob bytes
s256_chain.source: PS serializes the approved mission once and persists those exact bytes
s256_chain.detail: s256 = BASE64URL(SHA-256(bytes)). The PS returns the same bytes base64url-encoded as the `mission` member, so the agent can recompute the digest itself.

s256_chain.label: mission_s256 in the person token
s256_chain.source: PS stamps it when the agent names the mission at the person token endpoint
s256_chain.detail: The agent asks for a person token with mission_s256; the PS verifies the mission exists, is active and belongs to this agent, then puts the value in the token.

s256_chain.label: mission_s256 in the resource token
s256_chain.source: Resource copies it out of the person token it verified
s256_chain.detail: REQUIRED when the person token carried one — a resource MUST NOT omit it. presented_jti names the exact token it was copied from.

s256_chain.label: mission_s256 in the auth token
s256_chain.source: Issuer copies it from the resource token
s256_chain.detail: The resource reads the mission only here. It never arrives as a header and is never agent-asserted.
